cover.subtitle: Error handling in Java 25 with dmx-fun: one method, rewritten until its signature stops lying.
hook.question: What happens when this fails?
hook.answer: Three answers, none of them in the signature: an exception, a null, an Optional nobody checks.
ch0.caption: Read only the signature: it promises an Enrollment. The body has three throws, a null and a wrapped cause.
error.caption: Five things that can go wrong, written once, as data. Each record carries what the caller needs to act.
signature.caption: Same checks. Each failure is now a value the caller receives, not an event the caller has to catch.
switch.caption: No try, no null check. Delete one case and the class stops compiling.
tracks.caption: On the success track each step feeds the next. The first failure switches tracks and skips everything after it.
railway.caption: Each step returns a Result. flatMap passes a value forward or lets an Err travel untouched. Nobody checks isOk() in between.
byhand.caption: Three independent rules. combine runs them all and merges the failures, so a form with three problems reports three messages.
guards.caption: The same rules as values: written once, composed with allOf, reused anywhere. check returns every failure at once.
bridge.caption: The bridge from Validated to Result: all the form messages travel as one InvalidForm error on the failure track.
why.intro: Not a port of another language's library. Java 25 is the baseline, and the types are the ones the language now makes cheap.
why.vavr: Vavr and Arrow fill the same gap for Java 8 and Kotlin. This library assumes sealed interfaces, records and pattern matching already exist.
integrations.caption: Each integration is an optional module with its framework as a compile-only peer. You bring the version; CI tests the matrix.
status.caption: The error type is sealed, so this switch is exhaustive: add a case to EnrollmentError and it will not compile until it has a status.
metrics.caption: Failures with names need no log parsing. The tag is the record's simple name, so PaymentFailed shows up next to Waitlisted.
demo.intro: A Spring Boot 4 controller returns Option and Result directly. No ResponseEntity, no exception handler, no JSON code.
demo.fallback: If the network or Docker fails: the same four requests, recorded.
cast.caption: Recorded against the same sample. Space plays, the arrows seek; narrate over it as over the terminal.
adopt.caption: Adopt at one boundary, never big-bang. Translate at the seams with toResult, mapError and getOrElse; the rest of the code does not notice.
contribute.try: Try it on one endpoint and open an issue telling us which error type you designed. Design feedback is the most valuable kind.
contribute.gfi: Pick a good first issue. Each one names the files to touch and what done looks like.
contribute.integrations: Write an integration we lack: Micronaut, Helidon, the HTTP client you use every day.
contribute.posts: Tell your adoption story as a guest post on the blog.
closing.ask: Try it on one endpoint. Open an issue telling us which error type you designed.
closing.tutorial: The tutorial: this example, ten chapters
qa.immutability.a: Allocation is cheap on a modern JVM: escape analysis and thread-local allocation absorb most of it. Measure before you mutate; the profile rarely points here first.
qa.checked.a: They are not values. No map, no flatMap, no lambdas, no composition. Result is the same idea, and the compiler can follow it through a pipeline.
qa.kotlin.a: Same gap, different language. If you can switch languages, do. If your codebase is Java, this is the idiomatic answer on Java 25.
qa.caption: The three posts have the long answers.
backup.intro: If there is time, or if someone asks what happens after chapter 5.
either.caption: A full course is not a failure; it is a waiting list. Two legitimate answers, so the success value becomes Either. The failure track only lost a case that never belonged there.
nel.caption: Two cardinality rules move from comments into types. A course has at least one schedule; a cohort worth mailing has at least one student. Nobody writes isEmpty() for a case that cannot happen.
